question: The current agreement for the mutual recognition of academic qualifications between Greece and Cyprus does not encompass a range of academic institutions with accredited and recognised programmes of study, which maintain high educational standards and are fully accredited by the competent authority, namely the Cyprus Agency of Quality Assurance and Accreditation in Higher Education (CYQAA).

This exclusion limits the opportunities for graduates and diminishes the value of qualifications obtained from these institutions for numerous students and professionals who wish to pursue further education or career opportunities in Greece and other EU Member States. In view of the above, the Commission is asked: 1.
Whether the above-mentioned mutual agreement is in line with EU law?

Given that the principle of fair recognition of qualifications across EU Member States is fundamental to fostering an inclusive, knowledgeable, and interconnected Europe, does it intend to make recommendations to the parties involved for amending the agreement?

Will it review the current mutual agreement between Greece and Cyprus and make sure that all titles accredited/recognised by the CYQAA and the Cyprus Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth, are recognised by all parties involved?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.3.2024) In line with Article 165 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union1, Member States are solely responsible for the content of teaching and the organisation of their education systems. Consistent with this, the primary responsibility for the mutual recognition of academic qualifications rests with national authorities.

The written question asked by the Honourable Member, therefore, does not fall within the remit of binding EU law or the review competence of the Commission. The Commission remains committed to strengthening the mutual recognition of academic qualifications within the EU, while fully respecting the competences of the Member States.

The Commission is working with Member States and stakeholders on developing a voluntary European quality assurance and recognition system. One of the objectives of this initiative will be to ensure automatic recognition of qualifications made in the EU, building on non-legally binding commitments made by education ministers in the Council since 20182 and more recently in 20233.
